q: A bot replies to direct messages but never responds when @mentioned in a group. What is the likely cause?
options: The bot token expired
groupPolicy is set to disabled
USER.md is missing
Streaming is enabled for the channel
explanation: DMs working rules out the token; the failure table maps this symptom to a misconfigured groupPolicy that should be mention. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.9)

q: Why does the book recommend HMAC-SHA256 over a bearer token for webhook authentication?
options: It is faster to compute
It works without a shared secret
It accepts calls from any source
It binds the signature to the payload content
explanation: A static bearer token proves nothing about the payload; an HMAC signature is computed over the content itself. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.2)

q: Which context component belongs to the variable suffix rather than the stable prefix?
options: Session conversation history
Tool schemas
MEMORY.md
Yesterday's daily log
explanation: Steps 8-9 (history and the incoming event) change each turn; steps 1-7 form the cacheable prefix. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.3)

q: SOUL.md is accidentally deleted from the workspace. What does the runtime do by default?
options: Refuses to start
Loads a built-in default SOUL.md
Skips the file silently; the agent responds without the intended behavioral constraints
Discards all incoming events
explanation: Missing files are skipped without error, so the book suggests an AGENTS.md check that alerts the operator. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.3)

q: Where should API credentials used by a tool live?
options: In MEMORY.md
In environment variables accessed by the tool implementation
In USER.md
In the tool's SKILL.md
explanation: Anything in workspace context files is readable by the model and potentially exposed through injection. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.3)

q: SOUL.md and AGENTS.md give conflicting guidance on an edge case. Which governs?
options: SOUL.md, because it establishes the interpretive frame
AGENTS.md, because it is more specific
Whichever file was edited most recently
Neither; the model always asks the user
explanation: The model treats SOUL.md as the frame for interpreting the operational rules in AGENTS.md. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.5)

q: What is the order of OpenClaw's tool execution pipeline?
options: Permission check, execution, schema validation, sandbox check, result normalization
Sandbox check, schema validation, execution, permission check, result normalization
Execution, result normalization, permission check, schema validation, sandbox check
Schema validation, permission check, sandbox check, execution, result normalization
explanation: Arguments are validated first, permissions and sandboxing are resolved before execution, and output is normalized last. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.6)

q: A SKILL.md says never to delete events organized by others, yet after processing a crafted email the agent deleted one. What is the most robust fix?
options: Reword the SKILL.md rule more forcefully
Add a second calendar tool
Enforce the organizer check inside the tool implementation
Disable prompt caching
explanation: SKILL.md notes are only interpreted by the model; a code-level check refuses the call even if the model is manipulated. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.6)

q: An operator finds an entry in MEMORY.md they never authorized; it appeared after the agent processed an email. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: Memory poisoning through injection; remove the entry and restrict memory-write sources in AGENTS.md
Slow daily log promotion; promote entries manually
Session history truncation; raise the hard threshold
Wrong scheduler timezone; fix the cron setting
explanation: The failure table maps unexpected MEMORY.md entries to injection, fixed by removal plus write restrictions. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.9)

q: A Telegram user receives a burst of partial, incomplete messages for each reply. What is the likely cause?
options: The character limit is set too high
Streaming is enabled on a non-streaming surface
dmPolicy is set to open
parseMode is set to mrkdwn
explanation: Streaming to a messaging app produces message fragments; the book enforces non-streaming in both config and AGENTS.md. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §2.8)
